title: Tennis: Speed and Spin
summary: How tennis players use powerful serves and different kinds of spin, and how the court surface changes the way the ball bounces.
poll: In tennis, spin is more important than speed.

versions.title: Hit, Zip, Spin
versions.text:
Tennis is a fast game. Two players stand on a court. A net is in the middle. Each has a racket. They hit a ball back and forth.

The ball is made of rubber. It has fuzz on it. Most balls are bright yellow. That way, they are easy to see.

Each point starts with a serve. A player tosses the ball up. She hits it hard. A top serve is as fast as a race car!

Good players make the ball spin. They brush up on the ball. The top of the ball spins on. The air pushes it down. It dips into the court. Then it has a high bounce.

They can cut down on the ball, too. Now it spins the back way. The ball floats. It stays low. It skids when it lands.

Spin helps a player win. It makes the ball hard to hit back.

Riyadh is a city in Saudi Arabia. It now holds a big event. The best women play there.

versions.title: Tennis: Speed and Spin
versions.text:
Tennis is one of the fastest games in the world. Two players, or two teams of two, stand on a court with a net across the middle. Each player swings a racket and tries to hit the ball over the net so that the opponent cannot return it.

A tennis ball is made of hollow rubber and covered with a fuzzy cloth called felt. Most balls are bright yellow, so players and fans can see them easily as they fly.

Every point begins with a serve. The player tosses the ball high and strikes it with great force. The best players can serve at more than 200 kilometers per hour, which gives the opponent less than a second to react!

Speed is not the only weapon, though. Good players also make the ball spin. To hit topspin, a player brushes up the back of the ball with the racket. The top of the ball spins forward, and the air pushes the ball down. As a result, it dips sharply into the court and then kicks up in a high bounce.

To hit backspin, a player slices down under the ball, so it spins the other way. This ball floats, stays low, and skids when it lands.

The surface of the court matters, too. On grass, the ball skids and stays low, but on clay, it slows down and bounces higher.

Spin helps a player win points, because it makes the ball hard to hit back.

In Saudi Arabia, the city of Riyadh now hosts the WTA Finals, where the best women players of the year compete.

versions.title: Tennis: Speed and Spin
versions.text:
Tennis is one of the fastest sports in the world. Two players, or two teams of two, stand on a rectangular court with a net stretched across the middle, and each competitor swings a racket and attempts to hit the ball over the net so that the opponent cannot successfully return it.

A tennis ball consists of hollow rubber, filled with pressurized air, and covered with a fuzzy fabric called felt. Most balls are fluorescent yellow, which makes them easily visible to players and spectators as they travel across the court.

Every point begins with a serve, the most powerful shot in tennis; the player tosses the ball high and strikes it with tremendous force, and the best professional players can serve at more than 200 kilometers per hour, which gives the opponent less than a second to react.

Velocity is not the only weapon, however, because skilled players also generate spin; when the strings brush across the ball, friction grips the felt and sets the ball spinning. To produce topspin, a player brushes up the back of the ball, so the top of the ball rotates forward, and this rotation creates higher air pressure above the ball than below it, a phenomenon scientists call the Magnus effect, and that pressure difference pushes the ball downward, so its trajectory curves sharply into the court before the ball kicks up in a high, aggressive bounce.

To produce backspin, a player slices down underneath the ball, which makes it rotate in the opposite direction; this ball appears to float through the air, remains low, and skids when it lands, frequently forcing the opponent to bend down awkwardly.

The surface of the court is also significant. On grass, the ball skids and stays low, while on clay it decelerates and bounces higher, so competitors must modify their strategy for each different surface, and only the most adaptable athletes succeed everywhere. Officials even test tournament balls by dropping them from a standard height, because a ball that bounced too high or too low would change the character of the competition.

Spin helps a player win points, because it makes the ball's path difficult to predict and challenging to return.

In Saudi Arabia, the city of Riyadh now hosts the WTA Finals, a prestigious championship where the most successful women players of the year compete against one another.

versions.title: Tennis: Speed and Spin
versions.text:
Tennis is one of the fastest sports in the world. Two players, or two teams of two, stand on a rectangular court with a net stretched across the middle, and each competitor swings a racket and attempts to hit the ball over the net so that the opponent cannot successfully return it.

A tennis ball consists of hollow rubber, filled with pressurized air, and covered with a fuzzy fabric called felt. Most balls are fluorescent yellow, which makes them easily visible to players, officials, and television audiences as they travel across the court.

Every point begins with a serve, the most powerful shot in tennis; the player tosses the ball high and strikes it with tremendous force, and elite professional players can serve at more than 200 kilometers per hour, which gives the opponent considerably less than a second to react.

Velocity is not the only weapon, however, because skilled players also generate spin; when the strings brush across the ball, friction grips the felt and sets the ball rotating. To produce topspin, a player brushes up the back of the ball, so the top of the ball rotates forward, and this rotation creates higher air pressure above the ball than below it, a phenomenon scientists call the Magnus effect, and that pressure difference pushes the ball downward, so its trajectory curves dramatically into the court before the ball rebounds in a high, aggressive bounce.

To produce backspin, a player slices down underneath the ball, which makes it rotate in the opposite direction; this ball appears to float through the air, remains low, and skids when it lands, frequently forcing the opponent to bend down awkwardly and hit upward.

The surface of the court is also significant. On grass, the ball skids and remains low, while on clay it decelerates and bounces higher, so competitors must modify their strategy for each different surface, and only the most adaptable athletes succeed everywhere. Before major tournaments, officials examine the balls by dropping them from a standardized height, because a ball that rebounds excessively or insufficiently would alter the entire character of the competition.

Spin therefore helps a player win points, because it makes the ball's path unpredictable and considerably more challenging to return.

In Saudi Arabia, the city of Riyadh now hosts the WTA Finals, a prestigious championship where the most successful women players of the year compete against one another.

HIGH.prompt: Using the words friction, rotation, and pressure, explain the science of how topspin helps a tennis player keep a fast shot inside the court.
checklist: I explained the steps of topspin in order.
I used friction, rotation, and pressure correctly.
I connected the science to winning points.
HIGH.modelAnswer: Topspin helps a tennis player keep a fast shot inside the court through a careful combination of friction, rotation, and air pressure. As the racket's strings brush up the back of the ball, friction between the strings and the felt causes the ball to spin forward in rapid rotation. This forward rotation changes the air pressure around the ball, creating more pressure on top and less underneath, which pushes the ball downward and makes it dip sharply into the court even when hit with great force. Because of this dip, a player can swing hard for speed while topspin still pulls the ball back down to land safely inside the lines.
